newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs on Wednesday were seen selling steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by sluggish pork demand and an increase in hog marketings on Tuesday, livestock dealers said.
Several packer buyers said they were out of the market by 1200 CST on Tuesday after buying the hogs they needed for Wednesday's slaughter.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs at the plant could range from $48.50 to $49.00 and top Illinois prices at plants were seen at $47.50 to $48.00, sources in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $48.00 to $48.50, sources there said.
Ideas of weaker hog prices were tied to the inability of pork prices to recover from their current slump.
Fresh pork loin prices at midday were quoted weak to $3.00 per cwt lower, hams steady to $1.00 lower, pork bellies steady and lean trimmings were $2.00 to $5.00 lower, USDA said.
Larger-than-expected hog marketings Monday and estimates for relatively large movement Tuesday lent further weakness to price outlooks for Wednesday cash hog prices, dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog movement on Monday totaled 106,000 head, above USDA's estimate of 100,000, USDA said. Tuesday's estimate was 105,000 head versus 102,000 a week ago and 98,000 a year ago.
